    {
      "name": "Regime-Switching Holarchy: Tissue Learns Whether to Consensus, Union, or Gossip",
      "levels": ["tissue", "organ", "family"],
      "mechanism": "Each 6x3 tissue block first runs two cheap probes: (a) per-member competence on a small brightness-only text (known from E1 to give ~0.30), and (b) pairwise disagreement entropy across 3 independent Jev noul votes on its patch. A Jev choice then selects one of three regimes for that tissue: CONSENSUS (E2 jury-style agreement on the reconstruction) when members are competent AND agreement is high; UNION (E4-style OR of independent senses) when members are weak but disagree; SILENT (no propagation, like the 'empty sky' case in E1) when both competence is low AND entropy is high. Organs then aggregate tissue outputs without a centre, only via the regime labels each tissue broadcasts.",
      "jev_role": "Performs the typed choice that picks the regime per tissue based on the two probe answers; also runs the noul votes inside CONSENSUS and UNION regimes.",
      "hypothesis": "Regime-switching beats any single regime averaged across frames. Falsified if pooled fidelity (averaged over the brightness/edge/motion frame mix used in E1+E3) is NOT significantly above the best single-regime baseline of 0.354 (E2 jury) — measured as pooled fidelity with bootstrap 95% CI excluding the 0.354–[0.016,0.089] band.",
      "builds_on": "E1 (tissue-level 'what' dies at 0.03–0.24; gossiping beliefs into empty sky hurts), E2 (consensus +0.053 when members competent), E4 (union +0.046 when members weak). The provisional principle is the explicit motivator.",
      "cost": "2 probe questions + 1 regime-choice per tissue per frame, plus the chosen regime's cost. On 8 frames × 18 tissues = ~144 regime choices, ~300ms each on Jev ≈ a few minutes; well within a week.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Classic ML picks one aggregation (average, max, vote) at design time. Here the aggregation rule is itself a per-region typed decision, so the holarchy adapts its own social protocol to local competence — closer to a tissue choosing whether to be a neuron, a glial cell, or silent."
    },
    {
      "name": "Perspective Speciation: Lineage That Splits When Union Helps and Merges When Consensus Helps",
      "levels": ["family", "community"],
      "mechanism": "Start with a small 'founder' community of 6 perspective agents (brightness, edge, motion, braille, hybrid-A, hybrid-B from the E4 kaleidoscope setup). Each generation, each agent spawns 2 mutated children (byte-flips in the integer projector kernel, as in the Family Lineage idea). Children are scored on a calibration set spanning brightness-only, edge-glyph, and motion-heavy frames. Jev then issues a typed choice per parent: 'do your two children's error patterns correlate more than 0.5 (merge back, consensus regime) or anti-correlate (keep split, union regime)?' Agents that merge become one consensus voter (E2-style); agents that split become a union pair (E4-style). Over ~5 generations the community self-organises into specialists vs generalists.",
      "jev_role": "Scores each child against ground truth; emits the merge-or-split choice per parent based on child error correlation; aggregates the resulting mixed community on the held-out test set.",
      "hypothesis": "Self-speciated community fidelity on the E1+E3 mixed frame set exceeds a fixed 6-agent community and matches or beats the 0.354 E2 jury baseline on edge frames and the 0.31 E4 union on weak-signal frames simultaneously. Falsified if the speciated community is NOT significantly above 0.354 on edge frames (CI excludes the [0.016,0.089] jury-improvement band) OR not significantly above 0.31 on weak-signal frames (CI excludes E4's +0.046 union band).",
      "builds_on": "E2 (consensus works when members competent), E4 (union works when members weak and err differently), and the 'Family Lineage of Projector Kernels' first-round idea which proposed mutation without the merge/split choice.",
      "cost": "6 founders × 2 children × 5 generations = 60 kernels to score; Jev scoring ~150ms × ~50 frames per kernel ≈ a few hours; runnable this week.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Classic ML has a fixed model class and fixed ensemble topology. Here the ensemble's topology (specialist vs generalist, consensus vs union pairs) is itself evolved by a typed Jev choice on error-correlation — the family is a self-organising taxonomy, not a hyperparameter sweep."
    },
    {
      "name": "Meta-Holo: The Research Loop Itself as a Holarchy (Tissues Propose, Family Selects, Community Validates)",
      "levels": ["community", "organism"],
      "mechanism": "Treat the 15 first-round ideas themselves as a 'cell layer'. Each idea is scored by 3 Jev noul probes on a shared held-out frame set (brightness text, edge-glyph text, motion-heavy text from E1+E3). A 'tissue layer' of 5 idea-clusters (jury / merger / growth / kaleidoscope / lineage) aggregates these via E2 consensus where intra-cluster agreement is high, E4 union where low. A 'family layer' then issues a single typed Jev choice per cluster: 'which cluster's pooled score is highest AND most generalisable across frame types?' The winning cluster's ideas are promoted to a 'community run' that actually executes the new experiments (e.g. the regime-switching holarchy above). The community's measured result then becomes the next round's calibration set — closing the loop.",
      "jev_role": "Runs the per-idea noul probes, the cluster-level typed choice, and the final community-selection choice; also scores the executed experiment's result against the prior calibration set.",
      "hypothesis": "The meta-holo picks an experiment whose measured fidelity exceeds the median of the 15 first-round ideas' individually-implemented versions, AND the chosen experiment's CI excludes the prior round's best (0.354 jury). Falsified if the chosen experiment's pooled fidelity is NOT significantly above 0.354 (CI overlaps the jury baseline), or if the meta-selection picks an idea whose standalone score is in the bottom half of the 15 (worse than random selection).",
      "builds_on": "E2 (consensus on competent reconstructions), E4 (union across weak senses), and the provisional principle that 'gossiping CHOICES coordinates' — here the choice being gossiped is which experiment to run next.",
      "cost": "15 ideas × 3 probes ≈ 45 Jev calls (~7s); plus the cost of the one chosen experiment (already budgeted in the other two ideas). The meta-layer itself is essentially free.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Classic ML has a fixed objective and a fixed search space chosen by the researcher. Here the research loop — idea generation, experiment selection, result interpretation — is itself a holarchy whose aggregation regime (consensus vs union vs silent) is selected by the same provisional principle the experiments test. The community is no longer just measuring a projector; it is the projector of its own next question."
    }
  ]
}

Fidelity vs truth: 0.30 on brightness-only text (a VLM reading the same text: 0.28), about 60% of the VLM on edge-glyph text (VLM 0.49-0.51 vs swarm 0.24-0.31). Tissues recognise background well (0.87-1.0) but what object they hold poorly (0.03-0.24): information dies at tissue-level 'what', not at organ assembly. Motion arrows survive (motion recall 0.40). Letting tissues hear neighbours' claims spread object labels into empty sky: background accuracy 0.87 -> 0.63, net fidelity down (not significant).
E2 community jury: three VLM critics reconstruct the same text. Believing the reconstruction the other two agree with most (no judge, no centre) beats averaging them: 0.354 vs 0.301 (+0.053, CI [0.016, 0.089]); a Jev judge choosing among them +0.042 (CI [0.006, 0.078]); oracle 0.433.
E3 guided growth: 8x4 tissues sense their patch of the real frame as numbers and choose how to draw themselves (tone / edges / braille / motion arrows); a second round hearing neighbours' CHOICES helps (+0.066, CI [0.002, 0.128]) but the mosaic only ties drawing everything with edges (0.328 vs 0.350, n.s.): mixing styles creates seams. Jev almost never chose the motion style (6 of 320 tissues).
E4 kaleidoscope: each tissue has two independent weak senses (raw text, numeric receptors). Asserting an object only where both agree collapses fidelity to 0.10 (they rarely agree); their UNION beats the better sense (+0.046, CI [0.019, 0.076]) and ties an oracle that knows which sense to trust.
